# Best Free SHSAT Practice Tests 2026: Official Digital + PDF


## TLDR


The best free SHSAT practice tests for 2026 are the four official digital tests on the NYC Public Schools SHSAT Practice Portal. They match the new computer-adaptive format with 50 ELA and 50 Math items, timed and untimed options, and answer explanations. Older official PDFs remain useful for content practice, and free third-party quizzes work for targeted drills, but neither replaces the official digital tests for format simulation. Use the official tests first, save at least one for the final weeks before test day, and build an error log after every practice session.


> **What Are the Best Free SHSAT Practice Tests for 2026?**

## What Changed for the 2026 SHSAT?


The fall 2026 SHSAT introduces computer-adaptive testing, making it important for students to practice with the current digital format rather than relying exclusively on older paper exams.

### Why the New Format Matters


Computer-adaptive testing adjusts question difficulty based on a student's responses. All students answer the same number of questions and are assessed on the same grade-level standards, but they may receive different items.


The digital format also makes interface familiarity important. Students should learn how to use the available tools, understand when answers can be changed, and practice working through question sets before test day.


### What Should Students Do Differently?


-


**Practice digitally:** Complete official digital practice tests rather than relying only on printed questions.


-


**Learn the navigation rules:** Do not expect to skip freely between questions or return to every earlier answer.


-


**Understand the question types:** Use the Student Readiness Tool to explore the available digital interactions.


-


**Review explanations:** Focus on why each answer is correct, not just whether the answer was right.


-


**Check official guidance:** Confirm current rules and accommodations through NYC Public Schools before test day.


For the authoritative exam description, visit the[official NYCPS SHSAT page](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/learning/testing/specialized-high-school-admissions-test) .


## SHSAT Practice-Test Glossary


Before comparing resources, it helps to know what the labels mean. Parents and students on Reddit frequently ask what makes a practice test “official” versus “SHSAT-style,” or what “adaptive” actually means in practice. Here are the terms that cause the most confusion.


### Official SHSAT Practice Test


A practice test released or hosted by NYC Public Schools. The current official portal has four full-length Grade 8 digital tests, Grade 9 mini practice tests, answer explanations, and timed/untimed options. If a student only has time for one free SHSAT practice test, make it an official one.


### Full-Length SHSAT Practice Test


A test long enough to simulate the real SHSAT session. For 2026, that means 50 ELA items, 50 Math items, and a 180-minute time limit. Be skeptical of pages that call a 15-question or 40-question set a “practice test.” Those are quizzes, not simulations.


Older official paper forms had 57 questions per section (114 total) and included grid-in math items. They remain useful for content, but their structure does not match the current exam. Kaplan’s free SHSAT pop quiz page, for example, still describes 57 ELA and 57 Math questions with grid-ins, which is the old format.


### Digital SHSAT Practice Test


A practice test taken on a computer interface rather than on paper. Digital practice is not a luxury. It trains screen reading, answer-lock behavior, on-screen tool use, and the stamina of staring at a screen for three hours.


Practitioners have noticed that digital navigation itself eats into testing time. Bell Curves, a test-prep company, shared on LinkedIn that clicking, scrolling, and confirming answers could consume 16 to 24 minutes of the 180-minute exam. That is time most students do not plan for, and it is exactly the kind of “digital friction” that only shows up during realistic screen-based practice.


### Computer-Adaptive Test (CAT)


A test where question difficulty adjusts based on the student’s performance as it progresses. The fall 2026 SHSAT is adaptive. This is not the same thing as “digital.” A test can be digital without being adaptive (the same fixed questions on a screen), and an adaptive test does not necessarily look different from a regular digital one.


Old strategies like “skip the hard ones and come back” are gone. Students must commit to an answer and move forward.[Greg’s Tutoring warns](https://www.gregstutoringnyc.com/adaptive-shsat-faqs/) students to be cautious with third-party adaptive exams because question quality varies, and the adaptive SHSAT should not be assumed to work like the digital SAT.


### Technology-Enhanced Items (TEIs)


Question formats beyond basic multiple choice: drag-and-drop, select-all, clickable text selection, dropdown menus, numeric entry. A paper PDF cannot train these interactions. Students need the official digital portal or the Student Readiness Tool to get comfortable with them before test day.


### Timed vs. Untimed Practice


The official portal offers both modes. Timed mode runs a 180-minute countdown and auto-submits when time expires. It cannot be paused. Untimed mode removes the clock and is useful for first exposure, tool exploration, and reviewing explanations while working.


Use untimed for learning. Use timed for simulation. Do not start a timed official test unless you have three uninterrupted hours.


### Diagnostic Test


A practice test taken early in preparation to identify strengths and weaknesses. A good diagnostic leads to a study plan, not just a number. The concept works the same way across standardized tests, whether you are preparing for the SHSAT or taking[a diagnostic test](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/diagnostic-test) for the SAT. Identify weak spots first, then target them with focused practice.


### Answer Explanations


Written reasoning explaining why the correct answer is right and why wrong choices are wrong. Tests without explanations are significantly weaker for self-study. The official portal provides explanation documents for each practice form.


Practitioners on Reddit note that the official post-test report is helpful but minimal. It shows which items were correct or incorrect, but students must manually cross-reference with the separate explanation documents. Plan for this extra step before you start.


### Raw Score and Scaled Score


Raw score is the number of questions answered correctly. Scaled score adjusts raw performance through calibration and normalization, which NYCPS redoes each year. A raw score of 45 out of 50 on a practice test does not correspond to a fixed scaled score.


Track raw-score trends over time rather than fixating on a single number. Understanding[how score conversion works](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/score-calculator) on standardized tests helps set realistic expectations for what practice results actually mean.


### Cutoff Score


The composite score of the last student admitted to a particular Specialized High School in a given admissions cycle. Cutoffs are not set in advance. They result from seat availability, applicant scores, and preference order. Historical cutoffs provide rough context but should never be treated as guaranteed targets.


### Grade 9 Mini Form


A shorter official practice set for students taking the Grade 9 SHSAT for 10th-grade entry. NYCPS says Grade 9 mini forms should be used together with the Grade 8 full-length tests, not instead of them. Grade 9 resources are thinner than Grade 8, which is a common source of frustration.


### Student Readiness Tool (SRT)


A tutorial for learning the digital test interface and tools: highlighting, answer eliminator, notepad, and item interactions. This is not a content test. Use it before your first full digital practice test to reduce tool anxiety and learn the navigation rules.

## Best Free SHSAT Practice Tests, Ranked by Purpose


Not all free SHSAT practice tests serve the same purpose. Some simulate test day. Others drill content. Some are genuinely free. Others are trials that quietly convert to paid subscriptions. This ranking separates them by what they are actually good for.


### Tier 1: Official NYCPS Digital Practice Tests (Best Overall)


**What you get:** Four full-length Grade 8 digital tests (two with new content for the year), Grade 9 mini forms, timed and untimed options, the choice to start with ELA or Math, answer explanations, and a post-test summary showing which items were correct or incorrect.


**Why these are the best free SHSAT practice tests:** They come from the test maker. They use the current digital interface, the 50+50 question structure, and forward-only navigation. No login or payment needed.


**Practical details:**


-


Timed mode cannot be paused. Block out three uninterrupted hours.


-


Print or save the summary report immediately after submitting. You may not be able to access it later.


-


Test items are in English only (translated directions and footnotes are available for eligible ELLs).


-


Text-to-speech is only for students with approved accommodations.


**Where to find them:** The[official practice portal](https://nycshsat.myassessmentsupport.com/practice-tests/) is the starting point for any serious SHSAT prep.


### Tier 2: NYC Guide to the SHSAT for 2027 Admissions


This is not a practice test, but it is the single best reference for understanding what the SHSAT actually measures and how the exam works. The official guide defines the 2026 format, gives preparation advice, explains navigation limits, lists test-day rules, and includes sample ELA and Math questions with explanations.


Read it before taking your first full practice test. It will make every other resource more useful.


### Tier 3: Official PDF Archives (Best for Extra Content)


Several tutor-run sites compile every official SHSAT form NYC has released over the years. The most useful:


-


[StuyPrep](https://www.stuyprep.nyc/16tests.html) hosts 24 official practice tests with answer explanations, plus notes about recycled questions across forms.


-


[Kenny Tan](https://kennytan.nyc/24-practice-tests-for-the-2026-shsat/) provides annotated archives with detailed format-change explanations and recycled-item tracking.


-


Steps Tutoring and The Exam Coach offer clean downloadable PDFs of prior-year tests from 2018 onward.


**The caveat:** Older forms have 57 items per section, include grid-in math, and allow free navigation. Use them for content volume and endurance practice. Do not treat them as current-format simulation.

## “Free” Does Not Always Mean “Full-Length”


The word “free” covers a wide range in SHSAT prep:


-


**Official free:** No login, no payment, full-length test from the DOE.


-


**Free quiz:** Useful for quick practice, but 15 or 40 questions is not a simulation.


-


**Free diagnostic:** May give a score but lock detailed reporting behind a paywall.


-


**Free trial:** Full access for a limited time, then auto-converts to a paid subscription.


-


**Free PDF:** Content practice on paper, weaker for digital format training.


When evaluating any free SHSAT practice test, ask six questions. Does it match the 2026 format (50 ELA + 50 Math, 180 minutes)? Does it lock answers like the real test? Does it include TEI-style questions? Are answer explanations included, or just an answer key? Is it truly free, or is a trial or sign-up hiding behind the button? Does the page clearly state whether the test is adaptive or linear?

## How to Use Free SHSAT Practice Tests Without Wasting Them


Most families have access to four official digital tests and maybe a dozen older PDFs. That is a limited supply. Burning through everything in the first week is a common mistake, and one that Reddit’s r/SHSAT community warns about regularly. Here is a better approach.


**Step 1: Start with the Student Readiness Tool.** Spend 20 to 30 minutes learning the digital platform: highlighting, answer eliminator, notepad, and navigation. This prevents tool confusion from distorting your first real score.


**Step 2: Take one official test untimed.** If the student has never seen the SHSAT, an untimed first run removes time pressure and lets them focus on understanding question types and directions.


**Step 3: Take one official test timed as a baseline.** Quiet room. Three uninterrupted hours. Scrap paper. No calculator. Print or save the summary report the moment you finish.


**Step 4: Review with the answer explanations.** Do not just look at the score. Build an error log.

Review the error log weekly. If the same mistake appears repeatedly, focus your next study sessions on that skill before taking another full-length test.


Useful mistake categories to track: concept gap, misread question, calculation error, chose wrong passage evidence, grammar rule miss, time pressure, digital-tool issue, guessed without eliminating, locked in answer too fast.


**Step 5: Use older official PDFs for content volume.** After the first two official digital tests, switch to archived paper forms for topic-specific practice. These give you more ELA passages and more math problems to work through without burning your remaining digital tests.


**Step 6: Add short third-party drills for weak areas only.** If your error log shows a pattern (ratios, grammar conventions, evidence-based questions), use free quizzes for targeted reps. Do not use them as score predictors.


**Step 7: Save at least one official digital test for the final weeks.** This is your dress rehearsal. Take it timed, under realistic conditions, and compare the result to your baseline.


**Step 8: Review again.** The goal is not to take as many tests as possible. It is to learn from each one. This habit of diagnosing, targeting, and retesting works across every standardized test, from the SHSAT to the SAT. A[structured study plan](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/study-plan-generator) built around your specific weaknesses will always outperform random practice.


## How to Interpret Your SHSAT Practice-Test Score


A practice-test score is most useful when it shows which skills you have mastered and which need more work. It should not be treated as a guaranteed prediction of your official SHSAT score or school admission outcome.


### Track More Than the Number Correct


After completing a practice test, record these details:


What to Track


What It Tells You

Which questions need review


ELA performance


Whether reading comprehension or revising and editing needs attention


Math performance


Which mathematical concepts require more practice


Error type


Whether the problem came from a knowledge gap, misreading, calculation, or strategy


Time management


Whether you are working efficiently within the available time


Repeated mistakes


Which weaknesses remain after review


### Why Raw Scores Do Not Guarantee an Official SHSAT Score


A raw score counts correct answers. It is not necessarily equivalent to the scaled score used for admissions. The current SHSAT is computer-adaptive, so students should not assume that a raw score from a practice form can be converted directly into a reliable official score prediction.


Instead, compare results across practice sessions cautiously. Look for fewer repeated mistakes, stronger understanding of difficult concepts, and better familiarity with the digital interface.


### How to Turn a Practice Score Into a Study Plan


1.


Identify the questions you missed.


2.


Group mistakes by subject and skill.


3.


Review the official answer explanations.


4.


Practice the weakest skills with targeted questions.


5.


Revisit similar questions after studying.


6.


Use another full-length test later to assess progress.


The goal is not simply to increase the number of tests completed. It is to improve the underlying skills that caused each mistake.


## A Note for Grade 9 Retakers


Grade 9 students taking the SHSAT for 10th-grade entry face thinner resources. The official portal provides Grade 9 mini forms, but there are no full-length Grade 9 tests available.


On Reddit, a user specifically asked for free full-length Grade 9 SHSAT practice tests. The most helpful response recommended mastering the Grade 8 exams first and supplementing with the Grade 9 mini forms. That advice holds up. The Grade 8 tests cover the core ELA and Math skills through Grade 8 standards, and the Grade 9 mini forms add aligned content.


If you are a Grade 9 retaker, follow the same study sequence above, with one addition: take the Grade 9 mini forms after you have worked through at least two Grade 8 official digital tests.


## What Official Practice Tests Can and Cannot Tell You


Official SHSAT practice tests are the gold standard among free resources, but they are not crystal balls. Experienced tutors and Reddit users consistently make this point: official tests are representative of the real exam’s content and format, but they are not a limitless pool of real test-day questions.


They **can** tell you what question types to expect, how the digital interface works, where your content gaps are, whether your pacing is realistic, and how TEIs feel in practice.


They **cannot** tell you your exact scaled score on test day, the precise cutoff for your top-choice school, how the adaptive algorithm will respond to your specific performance pattern, or every possible question you might encounter.


Bell Curves reported on LinkedIn that they took the public SHSAT practice tests over 50 times with different performance patterns, and the questions did not change between runs. This confirms what NYCPS suggests: the official practice tests are format and content practice, not adaptive score predictors. Use them as your foundation, then build on that foundation with archived PDFs, targeted drills, and consistent review.


## Common Mistakes to Avoid


**Assuming every “digital” test is adaptive.** Digital means on a screen. Adaptive means the test adjusts difficulty. They are not the same thing, and many free SHSAT practice tests that call themselves “digital” present fixed questions on a website without any adaptive behavior.


**Using only old PDFs.** Older official PDFs are valuable for content practice, but they cannot train answer-lock navigation, on-screen tools, TEIs, or forward-only question flow.


**Not saving the summary report.** The official portal tells students to print or save the report after each test. Once you close the browser, it may be gone. This is an easy step to forget and a frustrating one to realize too late.


**Treating a raw score as a guaranteed prediction.** NYCPS calibrates and normalizes scores each year. A practice raw score is useful for tracking progress, not for calculating school odds.


**Trusting outdated pages without checking.** If a page says 114 questions, 57 per section, grid-ins, or “answer in any order,” it is describing the old format. The content may still be useful, but the structural details are wrong for 2026. Multiple threads in r/SHSAT show students confused by conflicting information across prep sites, especially around the adaptive transition. When in doubt, check the official NYCPS resources.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the best free SHSAT practice test for 2026?


The official NYCPS SHSAT Practice Portal. It offers four full-length Grade 8 digital tests with the current 50 ELA + 50 Math format, timed and untimed options, and answer explanations. No login or payment required.


### How many official SHSAT practice tests are available for free?


Four full-length Grade 8 digital practice tests and Grade 9 mini forms, all through the official NYCPS portal.


### Are old SHSAT PDFs still useful in 2026?


Yes, for content practice. The ELA reading skills and math concepts tested have not changed. But older forms use a different question count (114 instead of 100), include grid-in math, and allow free navigation, so they do not match the current format. Think of them as supplemental problem sets, not test-day simulations.


### Is the 2026 SHSAT computer-adaptive?


Yes. Beginning fall 2026, the SHSAT adjusts question difficulty based on the student’s ongoing performance. Every student still answers 100 total questions (50 ELA + 50 Math), but the specific questions will differ.


### Can you skip questions on the 2026 SHSAT?


Not in the old sense. Students must answer each question before moving forward. They can revisit answers within the same ELA passage set before submitting it, but after that, those answers are locked.


### Do free SHSAT practice tests predict my actual score?


They help track progress and identify weaknesses, but raw scores from practice do not directly convert to real scaled scores. NYCPS calibrates and normalizes scores annually, so treat practice results as directional feedback, not a guarantee.


### What should Grade 9 SHSAT students use?


Grade 8 full-length official digital tests plus the official Grade 9 mini forms. NYCPS says the mini forms should be used alongside the Grade 8 tests, not instead of them.


### What should I do right after finishing a practice test?


Save the summary report immediately. Review the answer explanations for every missed item. Log your errors by type and skill area. Use that log to plan your next week of study, then retest after meaningful practice.
